{"name": "charge-review", "steps": "Inputs: the developer's org or account id, the invoice (id or month), the lines and amounts they mean, request ids if they have them.

1. Identify the account. If you have neither org nor account id, ask_developer for org_id (plus invoice_id/invoice_month and line_items/amounts/request_ids in the same call if not given). lookup_account.
2. Check the billing channel and plan on the account.
   - Not billed directly by Redwood: search_knowledge for the procedure for that exact channel. A cloud marketplace (aws_marketplace, gcp_marketplace) and a reseller are different channels with different pages; apply only the one matching the console's billing_channel and don't borrow steps from the other. Support usually cannot credit or dispute these; tell the developer who bills them and where adjustments go. Do not open a credit or dispute.
3. Find the invoice: get_invoice (use lookup_account's invoice list to map a month to an id). Read console_confirmed_duplicates and same_amount_but_different_requests. If the developer gave request ids, get_usage them.
4. Classify:
   a. Console-confirmed duplicate: two lines on the same direct invoice billing the identical request ids. The duplicated line is the later line (duplicated_lines); credit that one, never the original.
   b. Look-alike: same amount/description but different request ids, or no second line. NOT a confirmed duplicate: say so plainly, with the console evidence (each line's request ids and times).
   c. Wrong rate/quantity/product, usage they don't recognize, retries/cancelled streams, token-count mismatch: search the token/usage pages first; if they explain it, explain and stop.
   d. Request to waive or reduce a correct charge (goodwill, exception, SLA credit): not Support's to issue. Load team-handoff.
5. For (a), search_knowledge for Support's current credit limit for duplicate charges and how it applies (per line, full line amount, no splitting). Read the approving document's status/date; drafts and proposals do not change the limit. If sources disagree on the limit (e.g. a draft, a thread or the developer cites a different figure), delegate to policy-researcher with the question and the dates before deciding. Compare the duplicated line's full amount with the limit.
   - Within limit: confirm_with_developer "Issue a credit note of $X (reason duplicate) on line L of invoice I". If yes: issue_credit_note for the full line amount with that reason, memo naming the request ids. Tell the developer the credit note id and amount. No handoff needed.
   - Over limit: do not credit and do not split. confirm_with_developer that you will open a dispute on line L and hand it to the owning team. If yes: open_dispute (reason duplicate_charge, the line, the request ids, submit=true), then load team-handoff and escalate with the dispute id.
6. For (b) and unexplained (c): gather intake (invoice, lines, UTC window, request ids, what they checked) with ask_developer, then load team-handoff for the owning team named in the routing policy.
7. Never promise a refund date or dispute outcome. If a write is rejected, read get_invoice to see the state before saying anything."}

Migration story for legacy customers (timeline & steps):

body: ## Scope
Customers who buy Redwood through a reseller receive the reseller's invoice, not Redwood's. This page covers disputes and credits on those invoices only. It is not the procedure for duplicate charges on a direct Redwood invoice; for those, use the support console credits and disputes page."}, {"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance/billing-adjustments-approval-matrix.json", "chunk": "3/6", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix", "status": "final", "date": "2026-02-03", "text": "## Approval matrix
| Adjustment | Who issues it | Limit and approver |
|---|---|---|
| Duplicate-charge credit (console-confirmed duplicate line on a direct invoice) | Support, from the support console | Up to $500 per duplicated line. Over that, Support opens a dispute and Billing Ops takes it |
| Billing-error correction other than a duplicate (wrong rate, quantity or product) | Billing Ops | Up to $2,000 per invoice; above that, the Controller |
| Refund of a paid invoice line after an approved adjustment | Billing Ops | Up to $5,000; above that, the Controller |
| Goodwill credit, waiver, or exception to a billing rule | Finance (FP&A) | Any amount, decided in FP&A's review. Support and Billing Ops route these requests and never issue them |
| SLA credit on a self-serve account | Finance (FP&A) | Self-serve plans carry no SLA. FP&A reviews any request as goodwill |
| SLA credit under a signed contract | Account team files the claim; Finance approves | Per the contract's SLA terms. No amount is promised before Finance's review |"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/billing-case-routing-and-handoffs.json", "chunk": "3/6", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Billing Support: Case Routing and Handoffs", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-06", "text": "(continued) ## When a case is needed
- Ask for the intake details before handing off. The receiving team works from the case and the conversation so far, so put everything the customer gave you in the case.
- If the customer doesn't have some of the details, hand off with what you have and note what's missing. Don't hold the case until they find them.
## Routing table
| Case | Owning team | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Disputed or duplicated line on a direct Redwood invoice | Billing Ops | Invoice number, the line(s), UTC window, request IDs |
| Refund request on a direct invoice line the customer says was billed in error | Billing Ops | Billing Ops confirms the charge and requests approval where needed |
| Invoice total doesn't match the customer's usage export | Billing Ops | Note the export's timezone and filters |
| Payment failures, holds, receipts | Billing Ops | |"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/billing-case-routing-and-handoffs.json", "chunk": "4/6", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Billing Support: Case Routing and Handoffs", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-06", "text": "(continued) ## Routing table
| Case | Owning team | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Meter discrepancy the related pages don't explain: request IDs whose billed tokens still don't match after the tokenizer, payload and retry rules are applied | Billing Engineering | Billing Eng checks meter correctness and hands any correction to Billing Ops |
| Request for a credit, goodwill credit, waiver, or removal of charges that were billed correctly (including retries), or an exception to a billing rule | Finance | The ask, the amount if given, and why. Applies even when Support has just explained that the charge is correct |
| SLA credit request on a self-serve account | Finance | Self-serve plans have no SLA; tell the customer, and still route the request. If the customer says a contract covers them, use the next row instead |
| SLA credit claim on an account with a signed contract | Account team | The CSM/TAM checks the contract's SLA terms and files the claim with Finance |"}]}

body: ## Purpose
This page provides standardized, copy/paste templates for public status page updates. The goals are:
- Reduce time-to-first-update (TTFU) without sacrificing accuracy.
- Keep language consistent across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private contexts.
- Share useful, actionable info (what’s impacted, where, what customers can do) without leaking sensitive details.
These templates are designed for the public status page update field and can be reused in Support macros and Console incident linking.
---"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/status-page-and-comms/incident-communication-templates.json", "chunk": "16/17", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Incident Communication Templates (Status Page + Customer-Facing Updates)", "status": "published", "date": "2026-01-09", "text": "## Checklist before you hit “Publish”
- Component(s) and region(s) match the taxonomy exactly.

- No promises on resolution time.
- Next update time is included for Investigating/Identified/Mitigating.
- If Sev0/Sev1: confirm approval requirements (see incident comms roles doc) and notify #support.
---
## Approval + coordination (summary)
- **Sev0/Sev1:** Comms Lead owns draft; IC approves content accuracy; Support Lead approval may be required before publishing depending on incident type and customer impact.
- **Sev2+:** Comms Lead or IC can publish, but still coordinate with Support if there is meaningful customer confusion.

body: ## Purpose
Saved replies keep common answers consistent. This guide covers how to write one; it doesn't set policy.
## Rules
- Lead with the answer, then the detail.
- Name the next step and who takes it.
- Never put an amount, a date or a limit in a saved reply: they change, and the policy pages are the source.
- Review each saved reply when the page it summarizes changes."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/status-page-and-comms/adr-014-status-page-component-mapping-source-of-truth.json", "chunk": "7/14", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "ADR-014: Status page component mapping – source of truth and change management", "status": "published", "date": "2025-12-06", "text": "## Review and ownership model

Open a case only when the customer asks for something Support can't do in the conversation, or reports a problem the related pages don't explain. Answering a question needs no case.
- Answer, don't hand off: how billed tokens are counted (model-native tokenizer, full request payload), why retries and cancelled streams are billed, and why the Console lags a few minutes are covered in the related pages. If one of them explains what the customer sees, explain it and stop there, even if the customer calls it a bug or double billing.
- If an older page says something different from the current one, explain the current behaviour and which page is current. That needs no case, even if the customer asks to report the old page as a bug.
- Questions about typical credit amounts, with no credit asked for, get the answer that there is no standard amount and that any amount is decided in Finance's review. No case."}]}
